item.title: Province supports more Island startups
item.description:
Province supports more Island startups jpranahan Mon, 08/10/2026 - 10:43

Five PEI companies are helping drive industry innovation with artificial intelligence.

Innovation PEI has provided close to $2.9 million in funding to 115 startups in the last 12 years to help them develop and transform their ideas into real market solutions. Each successful recipient receives up to $25,000 in seed capital through a competitive process twice a year.

As part of PEI’s Tech Week, organized by the Prince Edward Island IT Alliance, the province is pleased to announce its latest seed capital recipients. These five Island companies are leveraging advancements in technology, notably in artificial intelligence, to modernize industry, professional services, and showcase PEI’s growing technology ecosystem.

The recipients include:

  • Dylan Cooper of Boardwalk Inc.
  • Japneet Pal Singh Kalkat of Trailflow Systems Inc.
  • Paakow Wobil, Clinton Aghedo, Chrysler Hewlett, and Promise Ojo of Pentacore 
  • Parto Omidi and Soroush Izadan of Eidetic Design
  • Phil MacNevin of BuriedCandy Entertainment Inc.

The Ignition Fund is expected to open applications later this fall. 

Learn more about the Ignition Fund.

Quotes:

“No matter what industry you are in, you need innovation to grow. What our Island tech companies are doing is showing that PEI can come up with real, impactful technology solutions to help improve business operations. The Ignition Fund can be an important catalyst for any entrepreneur’s journey, and our government is proud to provide this much-needed capital to get entrepreneurs and their ideas to market.”

- Minister of Economic Development, Trade and Artificial Intelligence Jenn Redmond

“AI is changing how companies can compete, and these five are proof PEI founders are not waiting for permission. Tech is no longer only a sector; it is what the rest of the economy runs on. Almost every business on this Island has integrated technology solutions into their operations, from farms to fisheries to advanced manufacturing firms, and the companies building those tools are where new GDP comes from. The Alliance is here to support the people doing this work, whether they turn up at The Night Shift on a weeknight or push through 90 days in The Foundry Residency. Innovation PEI is an important partner to us, Island entrepreneurs, and our sector. Congratulations to all five teams.”

- Interim CEO of the PEI IT Alliance Ron Myers

“Receiving the Ignition Fund will help Trailflow turn early customer feedback into a stronger product for trucking companies across North America. It will help us improve AI agents that handle repetitive office work, from reading load documents to organizing paperwork and preparing invoices, while helping us reach more customers and grow export revenue from Prince Edward Island.”

- CEO of Trailflow Systems Inc Japneet Pal Singh Kalkat

 

Media contact:

Vicki Tse
Department of Economic Development, Trade and Artificial Intelligence
vickitse@gov.pe.ca 


Backgrounder:

Boardwalk Inc. – Dylan Cooper

Lightning Quote is a compliance verification software that uses AI to improve the estimating process for lightning protection systems. The platform creates a three-dimensional visual model showing how a proposed system will protect a building from lightning strikes. It can also review project specifications and architectural drawings, compare them against applicable industry codes and standards, and generate detailed compliance reports that identify potential issues and areas requiring attention. This helps lightning protection installers, architects and engineers prepare accurate designs, estimates, and documentation to save both time and money.

BuriedCandy Entertainment Inc. - Phil MacNevin

The Calling is a fast-paced, third-person, anime-style video game featuring popular video streamers as playable characters. Streamers participate as featured talent and receive a share of the revenue generated from their characters' in-game cosmetic items. The game also incorporates a rewards system designed to encourage ongoing player engagement and long-term retention. The Calling has won IndieDB's 5th Best Indie Game of 2025 and Best Studio award at the 2026 CGM Video Game Awards.

Eidetic Design – Parto Omidi and Soroush Izadan

An architectural digital content firm that provides Revit families, SketchUp models, renderings, datasheets, and other specification assets for building products. The platform helps manufacturers showcase their products to architects, designers, and specifiers by supplying accurate technical specifications increasing opportunities to be included in construction and development projects.

Trailflow Systems Inc. – Japneet Pal Singh Kalkat 

Trailflow is an agent-first logistics operating system for growing North American carriers and hybrid carrier-brokers. It gives back-office teams one live context for every load, where autonomous agents ingest emails and rate confirmations, coordinate dispatch, monitor exceptions, collect documents, and move work from intake to invoice and settlement. Trailflow turns fragmented tools and manual coordination into autonomous back-office workflows that execute routine work end to end.

Pentacore – Paakow Wobil, Clinton Aghedo, Chrysler Hewlett, Promise Ojo

WilowAI is an AI-powered personal study environment that transforms students’ uploaded notes, slides, and PDF documents into easy-to-use study materials, including summaries, flashcards, quizzes, and interactive AI tutor. The platform helps students stay organized with dedicated structured learning assets that includes progress tracking, achievement milestones, and reward features to help build consistent study habits.

item.title: Q and A with Scott Anderson, Irrigation Extension Specialist with the PEI Department of Agriculture
item.description:
Q and A with Scott Anderson, Irrigation Extension Specialist with the PEI Department of Agriculture jenniferdhogan Thu, 08/06/2026 - 11:35

What is the role of the Irrigation Extension Specialist? 

I work with irrigators across Prince Edward Island to support effective, responsible water use while helping maintain healthy crop production during dry conditions. I can provide guidance on the irrigation permitting process, irrigation system planning and implementation, water-use efficiency, and irrigation best management practices. My goal is to help producers make informed decisions that protect water resources while supporting productive and sustainable farming operations.

What is your background? 

I grew up in Morell on a mixed farm of dairy and potatoes. I always knew I wanted a career in agriculture, but I was also passionate about pursuing a degree in engineering. I ended up combining the two and became an agricultural engineer. 

After I graduated, I worked with the PEI Department of Agriculture as a Soil and Water Engineer, and later with Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada as the Regional Water Engineer, where I worked a variety of research projects surrounding sustainability, crop analysis, and water management. 

Why are you passionate about this topic? 

With a background in farming, I’m invested in making sure producers who are interested in learning about irrigation are choosing the right systems for their unique operations and using these systems to maximize sustainability and profitability for themselves and their families. 

What would you like Islanders to know about this service?  

With climate change, we are going to have periods where we need another source of water on the farm, so that producers can continue to grow food for their communities and take care of their livestock. 

This role works in collaboration with growers, government, and other industry partners to make sure that irrigators are using water resources responsibly and efficiently. Water management and hydrology are resources. When used correctly, there should not be a shortage.

Who is this service available to? 

This service is available to anyone in the Agriculture industry across the island who needs technical support regarding irrigation. This could be any commodity – grains, vegetables, potatoes, berries, specialized organic farms - you name it. In just a few weeks on the job, I’ve already had the opportunity to visit a variety of operations, each one unique, which is why it’s so important to take the time to learn about the many facets of irrigation before you dive in! 

How can producers contact you about this service? 

Producers can reach out by email or phone at:  atlanticwaterpei@gmail.com or phone at (902) 916-0603. 

We’ll start by discussing your goals, ideas, and irrigation needs, then arrange a farm visit. From there, I can provide technical guidance, help you navigate the permitting process, and draw on my experience to support the development of an irrigation system that’s right for you.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
